meta.description: Fictional knowledge base for the Tidewell Residential Waste Guide. Every corpus document, fine-tuning question and evaluation question is generated from this file. Facts are deliberately generic (no street addresses, phone numbers, staff names or exact times) so the model learns general disposal guidance rather than one memorized location.
notes: Items with "split": "heldout" must NEVER appear in the pretraining corpus or the fine-tuning set. They exist only to test whether the model can apply the general material rules to items it has never seen.
prep codes are canonical instructions; the corpus generator paraphrases them in many ways.

organization.name: Tidewell Waste & Recycling Services
organization.service_area: houses, townhomes and apartment buildings in the town of Tidewell
organization.purpose: Help residents decide how to sort, prepare and dispose of everyday household waste correctly.
organization.contact: Residents can contact the waste service through its website, its mobile app or its customer service line.
organization.out_of_scope: Commercial, industrial and construction waste are not covered by the residential guide.

recycling.name: recycling
recycling.summary: Clean paper, cardboard, rigid plastic containers, metal cans, foil, glass bottles and jars, and cartons.
rules: Everything must be empty, clean and dry.
Put recyclables in loose; never bag them.
Put caps and lids back on bottles, jugs and jars.
Flatten cardboard boxes so they fit with the lid closed.

organics.name: organics
organics.summary: All food scraps, food-soiled paper, and yard and garden trimmings.
rules: All food scraps are accepted, including meat, bones and dairy.
No plastic of any kind, including bags labelled compostable.
Line the kitchen pail with newspaper or a paper bag if you want to.

garbage.name: garbage
garbage.summary: Items that cannot be recycled, composted or dropped off, such as soft plastic, foam, diapers and pet waste.
rules: Bag garbage before putting it in the cart.
The lid must close; extra bags beside the cart may not be collected.
Never put hazardous waste, batteries or electronics in the garbage.

hazardous.name: household hazardous waste
hazardous.summary: Products that are flammable, corrosive, toxic or explosive, plus batteries and mercury-containing items.
rules: Never put hazardous waste in any curbside cart or pour it down a drain.
Bring it to a community drop-off depot or a household hazardous waste collection event.
Keep products in their original, labelled containers with lids sealed.
Small household quantities are accepted free of charge.

electronics.name: electronics
electronics.summary: Small items with a plug, cord or battery.
rules: Anything with a plug, cord or battery is electronic waste and never goes in a curbside cart.
Bring it to a community drop-off depot or a retailer take-back program.
Wipe personal data from devices before dropping them off.

bulky.name: bulky items
bulky.summary: Items too large to fit in a cart, such as furniture, mattresses and large appliances.
rules: Houses must book a bulky item pickup in advance; do not leave items at the curb without a booking.
Apartment and condo residents should use their building's designated bulky item area and check with the property manager first.
Usable furniture and appliances can be donated instead.

textiles.name: textiles
textiles.summary: Clothing, shoes, linens and other fabric items.
rules: Donate wearable and usable items.
Worn-out or torn textiles go to a textile drop-off bin, not the recycling cart.
Textiles must be clean, dry and in a tied bag.

takeback.name: pharmacy take-back
rules: Return unused or expired medications to a pharmacy.
Never flush medications or put them in any cart.
Sharps must be in a sealed, puncture-resistant container.

material_rules.text: Clean paper and cardboard go in the blue recycling cart.
Paper that is soiled with food or grease goes in the green organics cart.
Rigid plastic containers such as bottles, jugs, tubs and clamshells go in the blue recycling cart once they are empty and rinsed.
Soft or stretchy plastic such as bags, wrap, wrappers and pouches goes in the garbage, never in recycling.
Metal cans, tins and clean aluminum foil go in the blue recycling cart.
Glass bottles and jars go in the blue recycling cart.
Glass that is not a bottle or jar, such as drinking glasses, window glass and ovenware, goes in the garbage, wrapped for safety.
All food scraps, including meat, bones and dairy, go in the green organics cart.
Yard and garden waste such as leaves, grass and small branches goes in the green organics cart.
Small items with a plug, cord or battery go to an electronics drop-off.
Batteries of every kind go to a household hazardous waste drop-off, never in a cart.
Products labelled flammable, corrosive, toxic or poison go to a household hazardous waste drop-off.
Items too large to fit in a cart with the lid closed, including large appliances, are bulky items.
Clothing and fabric items are donated or taken to a textile drop-off.
Foam packaging, such as takeout containers and packing peanuts, goes in the garbage.
Medications and needles are returned through pharmacy take-back.
Plastic objects that are not containers, such as toys, hangers and toothbrushes, go in the garbage.
Small loose items like straws, plastic cutlery and loose caps fall through sorting equipment, so they go in the garbage.
Cartons for milk, juice, broth and plant-based drinks go in the blue recycling cart once they are empty and rinsed.
When you are unsure about an ordinary, non-hazardous item, put it in the garbage rather than risk contaminating the recycling.

prep_codes.caps_on: Put the cap or lid back on.
prep_codes.loose: Place it loose in the cart, not in a bag.
prep_codes.scrape: Scrape any leftover food into the green organics cart.
prep_codes.remove_liner: Remove the plastic liner and put the liner in the garbage.
prep_codes.unpackage: Take the food out of any packaging first.
prep_codes.cut_to_fit: Cut or break it so it fits in the cart with the lid closed.
prep_codes.bag: Put it in a tied bag before it goes in the cart.
prep_codes.wrap: Wrap it in newspaper or put it in a box labelled as broken glass.
prep_codes.cool: Let it cool completely for several days in a metal container.
prep_codes.original_container: Keep it in its original, labelled container with the lid sealed.
prep_codes.no_mix: Never mix it with other products.
prep_codes.tape_terminals: Cover the terminals with clear tape.
prep_codes.wipe_data: Back up and wipe your personal data first.
prep_codes.remove_batteries: Remove the batteries if you can and drop them off separately.
prep_codes.book_pickup: Book a bulky item pickup in advance, or use your building's bulky item area.
prep_codes.donate: If it is still in good condition, donate it instead.
prep_codes.clean_bagged: Make sure it is clean and dry and bring it in a tied bag.
prep_codes.sealed_container: Put it in a sealed, puncture-resistant container.
prep_codes.remove_decor: Remove all lights, decorations and the stand.
prep_codes.roll_tie: Roll it up and tie it.
prep_codes.remove_propane: Remove the propane tank first and take it to a hazardous waste drop-off.
prep_codes.extinguished: Make sure it is fully extinguished.

items.name: cardboard boxes
items.note: Small amounts of tape and shipping labels are fine to leave on.

items.name: office paper
items.note: Staples and paper clips can stay on.

items.name: junk mail
items.note: Envelopes with plastic windows are accepted.

items.name: paper bags
items.note: Paper bags can also be reused to line your kitchen organics pail.

items.name: paper egg cartons
items.note: Foam egg cartons are different and go in the garbage.

items.name: old books
items.note: Books in good condition should be donated; worn-out paperbacks can be recycled.

items.name: greeting cards
items.note: Cards with glitter, foil, batteries or sound chips go in the garbage.

items.name: wrapping paper
items.note: Plain wrapping paper is recyclable, but foil, glitter and metallic wrap go in the garbage. Ribbons and bows go in the garbage too.

items.name: shredded paper
items.note: Loose shreds jam sorting equipment, so shredded paper goes in the green organics cart instead of recycling.

items.name: receipts
items.note: Most receipts are printed on coated paper that cannot be recycled.

items.name: juice boxes
items.note: Push the straw inside the box.

items.name: pizza boxes
items.note: Greasy pizza boxes go in organics. A clean, grease-free lid can be torn off and recycled.

items.name: paper coffee cups
items.note: The cup has a plastic lining so it goes in the garbage, but the rigid plastic lid can be recycled.

items.name: shampoo bottles
items.note: Pumps contain metal springs, so remove pumps and put them in the garbage.

items.name: plastic takeout containers
items.note: Foam takeout containers are not recyclable and go in the garbage.

items.name: plastic plant pots
items.note: Knock out all the soil first.

items.name: plastic bags
items.note: Plastic bags tangle sorting machines. Reuse them as long as you can, then put them in the garbage.

items.name: packing peanuts
items.note: Many shipping stores will take clean packing peanuts for reuse.

items.name: plastic toys
items.note: Toys in good condition can be donated. Toys with batteries or cords are electronics.

items.name: garden hoses
items.note: Hoses wrap around sorting machines, so never put them in recycling.

items.name: toothbrushes
items.note: Electric toothbrushes are electronics.

items.name: disposable razors
items.note: Cover the blade so collection workers are not cut.

items.name: food cans
items.note: Put the lid inside the can and pinch the top closed so the sharp edge is covered.

items.name: aluminum foil
items.note: Scrunch clean foil into a ball at least the size of a fist. Foil covered in food goes in the garbage.

items.name: aerosol cans
items.note: Only completely empty aerosol cans go in recycling. Cans that still contain product are hazardous waste.

items.name: drinking glasses
items.note: Drinking glass melts at a different temperature from bottles and jars, so it cannot be recycled.

items.name: mirrors
items.note: Large mirrors that do not fit in the cart are bulky items.

items.name: incandescent light bulbs
items.note: Fluorescent and CFL bulbs are hazardous waste, and LED bulbs are electronics.

items.name: meat, fish and bones
items.note: Wrapping meat scraps in newspaper helps control odours.

items.name: dairy products
items.note: Pour small amounts of liquid milk down the drain; solids go in organics.

items.name: coffee grounds
items.note: Paper filters can go in with the grounds. Single-serve coffee pods go in the garbage.

items.name: cooking grease
items.note: Never pour grease down the drain. Let small amounts harden, or soak them up with paper towel, and put them in organics. Large amounts of used cooking oil go to a drop-off depot.

items.name: grass clippings
items.note: Leaving clippings on the lawn is an even better option.

items.name: leaves
items.note: Extra leaves can be set out in paper yard waste bags beside the green cart.

items.name: houseplants and cut flowers
items.note: Remove any plastic pot, wrapping or elastic bands first.

items.name: pumpkins
items.note: Remove candles and any paint or decorations.

items.name: holiday trees
items.note: Trees can be cut to fit in the green cart or set out whole on the holiday tree collection days announced each winter. Artificial trees go in the garbage or to bulky item pickup.

items.name: diapers
items.note: Diapers are not compostable even if they are labelled that way.

items.name: pet waste
items.note: Pet waste goes in the garbage, not the green organics cart.

items.name: ashes
items.note: Hot ashes can start cart fires.

items.name: wet wipes
items.note: Never flush wipes, even ones labelled flushable.

items.name: leftover paint
items.note: Completely empty, dried-out paint cans can go in the garbage.

items.name: propane tanks
items.note: Propane tanks can explode if crushed in a collection truck.

items.name: household batteries
items.note: Batteries can spark and start fires in carts and trucks.

items.name: lithium-ion batteries
items.note: Lithium-ion batteries are a leading cause of fires in collection trucks.

items.name: fluorescent tubes and CFL bulbs
items.note: They contain mercury, so do not break them.

items.name: mercury thermometers
items.note: Digital thermometers are electronics.

items.name: household cleaners
items.note: Leftover cleaners are hazardous waste. A completely empty, rinsed plastic bottle can go in recycling.

items.name: cell phones
items.note: Many retailers also take back old phones.

items.name: cords and cables
items.note: Cords tangle sorting machines, so never put them in recycling.

items.name: vapes
items.note: Vapes contain lithium batteries and must never go in the garbage.

items.name: mattresses
items.note: Keep mattresses dry before pickup.

items.name: refrigerators and freezers
items.note: Mention that it contains refrigerant when you book, and remove or tape the doors shut for child safety.

items.name: air conditioners
items.note: Mention that it contains refrigerant when you book.

items.name: clothing
items.note: Even torn or stained clothing can go to a textile drop-off bin.

items.name: medications
items.note: Never flush medications or put them in the garbage.

items.name: needles and sharps
items.note: Sharps containers can also go to a household hazardous waste drop-off. Never put loose needles in any cart.

facts.text: Your collection day depends on the area you live in; check the collection calendar for your area on the waste service's website or app.
The green organics cart is collected every week.
The blue recycling cart and the black garbage cart are collected on alternating weeks.
Set your carts out the evening before or early on the morning of your collection day.
Bring empty carts back from the curb by the end of collection day.
In a week with a public holiday, collection may be delayed by one day; the area calendar shows any changes.
Place carts at the curb with the wheels facing your home and the lid fully closed.
Leave space between carts and keep them clear of parked cars, mailboxes, poles and low branches.
Do not overfill carts; anything that keeps the lid from closing may be left behind.
In winter, place carts on a cleared surface, not on top of snowbanks.
If your cart was not emptied, first check that it was out on time and that it did not have a warning tag.
Report a missed collection to the waste service by the end of the next day through the website, app or customer service line.
If a cart is damaged, lost or stolen, request a repair or replacement through the waste service.
Apartment and condo residents use the shared bins in their building's waste room or collection area.
Sorting rules are the same in apartments as in houses: recycling, organics and garbage are kept separate.
Ask your property manager or building superintendent where the shared bins and the bulky item area are.
Never leave items in hallways, stairwells or beside a full bin; tell the property manager if bins are full.
Community drop-off depots accept household hazardous waste, electronics and other items that cannot go in carts.
Household hazardous waste collection events are also held at different locations through the year; dates are posted on the waste service's website and app.
Drop-off of household hazardous waste and electronics is free for residents in normal household quantities.
Transport hazardous products upright, sealed and separate from passengers, ideally in the trunk.
Check the waste service's website or app for the drop-off location nearest to you and its opening hours before you go.
Residents of houses book a bulky item pickup in advance through the waste service's website, app or customer service line.
Set booked bulky items at the curb the evening before the scheduled pickup day.
Apartment and condo residents take bulky items to the building's designated bulky item area; each building or complex has its own spot, so ask the property manager.
Leaving bulky items at the curb without a booking is treated as illegal dumping.
Furniture and appliances in good condition can be donated to charities and reuse centres instead.
Contamination means putting the wrong items in a cart, such as plastic bags in recycling or plastic in organics.
A contaminated cart may be left unemptied with a warning tag that explains the problem.
If your cart is tagged, remove the wrong items and set it out again on your next collection day.
Repeated contamination after warnings can lead to a fine.
Illegal dumping, including leaving items on curbs, in parks or beside shared bins without permission, can result in a fine.
Putting hazardous waste or batteries in any cart is prohibited because it endangers collection workers.
The best way to reduce waste is to avoid it: buy only what you need and choose reusable bags, bottles and containers.
Donate usable clothing, furniture, toys and household goods to charities, thrift stores or neighbours.
Repair items when you can instead of replacing them.
Plan meals and store food properly to cut down on food waste.
Residents with a yard can compost at home in a backyard compost bin.
A backyard compost bin can take fruit and vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, leaves and grass.
Keep meat, fish, bones, dairy and oils out of a backyard compost bin; put them in the green organics cart instead.
Mix wet green material with dry brown material like leaves, and turn the pile now and then.
To reduce odours, wrap food scraps in newspaper or keep them in the freezer until collection day.
Line your kitchen pail or green cart with newspaper or a paper bag; plastic bags of any kind are not allowed.
Keep the green cart lid closed and rinse the cart now and then to keep pests away.
When moving, start sorting early and donate what you no longer need.
Book a bulky item pickup well ahead of your move date, or ask your property manager about the building's bulky item area.
Flatten moving boxes for recycling, or pass them on to someone else who is moving.
Do not leave items behind at the curb or in the building when you move out.
After the holidays, plain wrapping paper and cardboard boxes go in recycling, while ribbons, bows and foil wrap go in the garbage.
Real holiday trees go in organics once lights, decorations and the stand are removed.
Leaves and garden waste can be set out in paper yard waste bags beside the green cart in spring and fall.
Correct sorting keeps recyclables clean so they can be made into new products.
Organics are turned into compost instead of going to landfill.
Wrong items, especially batteries and plastic bags, can damage equipment, start fires and injure workers.
When in doubt about an ordinary item, put it in the garbage; wishful recycling contaminates whole loads.
